groups.text: It is currently 17 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

In Meghalaya, the Khasi Students’ Union has submitted memorandums to all 36 elected representatives from the Khasi Hills. This move comes ahead of the autumn session of the Meghalaya Legislative Assembly beginning August 24, as the union presses legislators to bring five specific demands before the state government. The KSU also intends to submit these documents to 24 MLAs from the Garo Hills, arguing that representatives must address employment opportunities and challenges facing the Khasi community. In a separate shift for software developers, the llama.cpp project has released version 0.2.0. This update introduces consistent semantic versioning to simplify how downstream projects and users distribute the software. While technical users can still access bleeding-edge functionality through nightly build tags, these new stable version tags are designed to provide a more reliable release cadence for casual users and broader distribution.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports that Russia has lost approximately 1,475,270 troops since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. This total includes 1,240 casualties suffered by Russian forces over the past day alone. The material toll is equally steep, with losses including 12,292 tanks, 25,176 armored combat vehicles, and 48,382 artillery systems. Russia has also lost 474,641 unmanned aerial vehicles and 137,804 vehicles and fuel tanks. While Ukraine maintains operational secrecy regarding its own losses, the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimates that Russian casualties significantly surpass those of Ukraine. A January 2026 report from that think-tank suggests Ukraine likely suffered between 500,000 and 600,000 casualties through December 2025, with an estimated 100,000 to 140,000 killed in action. This creates a casualty ratio estimated at roughly two-to-one or two-and-a-half-to-one.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has vowed that Canada will match new United States tariffs dollar for dollar to protect domestic businesses and workers. This response follows the failure of trade negotiations, resulting in 50-percent duties on some Canadian products that took effect Saturday. These tariffs are expected to impact roughly 20 billion dollars of exports to the U.S., despite offers from Washington for reductions in sectors like aluminum and steel. In a separate geopolitical tension, Israel is expanding its presence in Syria, with an increase in incursions into Syrian territory since the fall of Assad. This includes recent attacks on a Syrian air force base and the detention of civilians. For example, in April 2024, Israeli soldiers arrested seventeen-year-old Saddam while he was feeding livestock on family fields near the Golan Heights, despite the family holding valid UN permits to work that land.

The election campaign in Saxony-Anhalt is drawing sharp scrutiny, particularly regarding the tactics of AfD lead candidate Siegmund. The Süddeutsche Zeitung notes that Siegmund’s approach mirrors a Trump-style playbook, emphasizing a bleak national outlook while positioning himself as the sole savior. He has criticized Berlin's policies as completely crazy and claimed that crime feels higher in the region, despite data showing that crime rates have actually fallen. While Siegmund presents himself as a smiling young manager to mask his party's extremist reputation, other politicians are suggesting harsher deterrents. Baden-Württemberg Finance Minister Danyal Bayaz of the Greens has proposed using financial reprisals against the state if voters help the AfD take power. This tension between populist campaigning and the threat of economic penalties highlights a deep divide in German politics. Meanwhile, reports indicate that German gas storage levels currently sit at only about 50 percent.

A developer has built a quantized large language model from scratch that can run on a standard laptop CPU without needing a GPU. The 250 million parameter model was trained on 30 billion tokens of fineweb and is quantized to under two bits. This allows the entire deployment to fit into 60 megabytes, requiring only about 80 megabytes of RAM to operate. To handle long contexts, the system keeps the most recent 2,048 tokens in fp16 while compressing older data to one bit on disk. This method enables the model to retrieve information from a disk cache of up to 100 million tokens, though it cannot reason over them due to budget constraints. The developer also replaced the standard embedding table with fixed 512-bit codes for its 131,000 tokens, resulting in zero trained parameters for the vocabulary and a deployment speed of roughly 400 tokens per second.

Russian strikes have killed at least two people in Ukraine early Saturday morning. In the capital city of Kyiv, military administrators reported a fire in a warehouse in the Darnytskyi district following a ballistic missile alert, leaving one person dead and several others injured. In Zaporizhzhia, regional head Ivan Fedorov confirmed that a Russian drone killed one man and wounded four people. These attacks follow a deadly Friday where Russian bombings killed at least 20 people across the country. The highest toll occurred in Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of President Volodymyr Zelensky, where a daytime drone attack on a busy shopping center killed 16 people and left 130 others injured. In other news from France, a new look at the city's cultural heritage reveals that Paris is home to six different representations of the Statue of Liberty, mirroring the famous monument in New York.

German authorities are investigating a cache of handguns and ammunition found in a forest near Berlin last year. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt says the suspect, who was arrested in Romania, is under investigation for espionage and planning a violent attack that endangers the state. While reports suggest the weapons were intended for assassinations on behalf of Russian intelligence, Dobrindt only stated that foreign powers could be involved. He noted that Germany is currently operating under a high threat level. In separate news from Pakistan, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has directed authorities to provide financial assistance to families hit by recent monsoon rains and floods. The premier ordered the delivery of essential food items to inaccessible areas and called for the urgent restoration of power supplies and roads. He also instructed the National Disaster Management Authority to remain prepared for further flooding.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will remain cloudy with temperatures between 17 and 19 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the summer holidays in Berlin and Uschi Bekaan's birthday.
Mail worth checking: Microsoft Rewards about Die Vorteile reißen einfach nicht ab.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
